description: Zone systems a prescription can name. An intensityZone carries a system and a label — "Z4" — and this registry is what makes that label mean the same thing in two applications. It defines the systems and their zone labels; it never carries the boundary values, which are personal and are caller context (RFC-006 §5.1).

entries.label: Five-zone heart rate
entries.description: The common five-zone model, expressed as percentages of maximum heart rate. The percentages are conventional; the athlete's maximum is not carried here.

entries.label: Three-zone heart rate
entries.description: The polarised-training model: below threshold, at threshold, above. Anchored on threshold rather than maximum, which is why it is a different system entry and not a coarser view of the five-zone one.

entries.label: Coggan seven-zone power
entries.description: Seven training levels expressed as percentages of functional threshold power. Widely used in cycling.

entries.label: Five-zone pace
entries.description: Pace zones anchored on threshold pace. Note that a higher zone means a lower time per unit distance — an implementation comparing zones numerically must not compare the paces themselves the same way.

entries.label: Ten-point perceived exertion
entries.description: A perceived-effort scale. Listed as a zone system because a prescription may name it the same way, but note that RPE as a *load* target is loadTarget.method "rpe" — this entry is for zone-style conditioning prescriptions.

entries.label: Borg 6–20 perceived exertion
entries.description: The original Borg scale. Present because 6–20 and 1–10 are both called "RPE" in the wild, and a document that does not say which one it means is ambiguous by exactly a factor of two.
